scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (SH-CS request).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-05).
59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) are ACTUAL-read type with no established cause yet (E-01).
41% of disputed bills (1240/3025) are ESTIMATED-read type (E-01).
Field manual-read route completion dropped from a 0.95 target to 0.88 across 9200 accounts in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-03).
Dispute ticket response times remain within SLA despite the volume surge (E-04).
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-05), not explained by slow ticket response (E-04: within SLA) or a tariff change (E-02: none logged). Field manual-read route completion dropped from a 0.95 target to 0.88 across 9200 accounts in the same window (E-03), pushing more accounts into estimate-substitution billing and accounting for the ESTIMATED-read share of disputed bills (1240/3025, 41%, E-01), though the majority ACTUAL-read share (59%) is still unexplained.

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-01 revised by E-09: E-01's observation still stands: 1240 of 3025 disputed bills are ESTIMATED read type and 1785 are ACTUAL. It no longer supports the premise's implicit sizing of how much of the ESTIMATED-read dispute share traces to the route-completion shortfall, since E-09's 320-account estimated count is far below the ~1104 accounts the 0.88/9200 shortfall would imply, so the route-completion-to-ESTIMATED-dispute link is weaker than PR-ROOT and PR-CHAIN-3 assume; the ACTUAL-read majority remains independently unexplained as before.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: SH-CS requested an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills; response speed is already within SLA (E-04) so this framing of the problem is rejected, and K-BILLWRITE prohibits automated bill writes regardless.

problem_definition_history.root_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-05). Response-speed (E-04: within SLA) and tariff-change (E-02, E-06: none logged) causes are ruled out. Billing validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 — exactly the surge's first month — changed the high-consumption check to compare raw register values against 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling (E-10), a mechanism that can mis-flag or mis-bill valid reads of either read type. Field route-completion shortfall (E-03: 0.88 vs 0.95 target) cannot explain the dispute buckets: only 320 accounts were actually marked estimated last cycle (E-09), far below the ~1104 the shortfall would imply, so field degradation is too small in magnitude to drive even the ESTIMATED-read bucket (41%, E-01), let alone the larger ACTUAL-read majority (59%, E-01). BV-17's unscaled-comparison defect is the best-supported mechanism for the surge spanning both buckets.

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a ticket-handling/response-speed problem, so an AI auto-answer agent (plus automated bill fixes) would resolve it, as SH-CS's request frames it.

H-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August introduced systematic bill errors (e.g., rejecting valid reads, forcing estimates), driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-DATA-GAP.statement: The nightly MDMS-to-billing export (H-MDMS-BILL) began failing or degrading around August, causing missing AMI reads and incorrect estimated bills.

H-FIELD-READ-DEGRADATION.statement: Manual meter-read completion or accuracy from the contracted field service (H-FIELD-BILL) degraded starting August, increasing estimated bills and disputes.

H-RATE-TARIFF-CHANGE.statement: Bills issued since August are largely accurate but a tariff/rate change raised amounts, producing legitimate customer disputes rather than billing errors.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: Field service has been short three readers since July (per SH-FIELD, unverified), causing routes to run late and resulting estimated bills for affected customers.

H-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-BUG.statement: BV-17's high-consumption check (deployed 2026-08-01) compares raw register values to 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling, plausibly causing valid reads to be mis-flagged or mis-billed, contributing to disputed bills in the ESTIMATED and/or unexplained ACTUAL bucket since the surge onset.

H-BV17-REJECTION-ESTIMATED-ONL.statement: BV-17's high-consumption check rejects AMI imports (import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), triggering immediate estimate substitution, so this mechanism structurally produces only ESTIMATED-type bills and cannot explain the ACTUAL-read dispute majority (1785/3025, E-01).

interpretation_history.interpretation: Of 3025 disputed bills, 1240 are ESTIMATED read type and 1785 are ACTUAL (59%). Most disputes are tied to bills built on actual reads, so causes that only produce estimated bills (missing AMI reads, failed manual reads) explain a minority of the dispute volume; something else drives the larger ACTUAL-read dispute bucket.

E-01's observation still stands: 1240 of 3025 disputed bills are ESTIMATED read type and 1785 are ACTUAL. It no longer supports the premise's implicit sizing of how much of the ESTIMATED-read dispute share traces to the route-completion shortfall, since E-09's 320-account estimated count is far below the ~1104 accounts the 0.88/9200 shortfall would imply, so the route-completion-to-ESTIMATED-dispute link is weaker than PR-ROOT and PR-CHAIN-3 assume; the ACTUAL-read majority remains independently unexplained as before.

billing-db.tariff_change_log shows 0 records, meaning no tariff or rate change was logged in the system since the dispute surge began. This removes the legitimate-rate-increase explanation for the ACTUAL-read dispute bucket E-01 highlighted.

Route-log data (E-03) shows manual-read route completion was 0.88 against a 0.95 target for 9200 accounts in the Aug-Sep 2026 window, confirming an actual degradation in field manual-read coverage coincident with the dispute surge. Per E-01, however, most disputed bills are ACTUAL-read type, so this field degradation (which would mainly drive estimated bills) likely explains only part of the surge.

re-read under E-09 (accepted premise check) — PR-ROOT: E-09 shows only 320 accounts were marked estimated in the last cycle, far below the ~1104 implied by the 0.88/9200 shortfall, so the route-completion drop explains less of the ESTIMATED-read dispute share than the root problem claims.; PR-CHAIN-3: E-09's 320-account estimated count is well below the ~1104 accounts the 0.88 completion shortfall would imply, so the magnitude of the route-completion-to-estimated-bill link is much smaller than this chain step requires.

CRM data shows ticket response handling is already fast and within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d SLA across 2440 tickets), so the dispute surge is not explained by slow ticket response — it points away from a response-speed problem and toward an underlying billing-accuracy cause.

Monthly dispute counts were ~600/month in June-July 2026, then jumped to ~1180-1260/month in August-September 2026, confirming the magnitude of the surge (roughly doubled) coincides with the window other evidence (E-01, E-03) already investigates. The observation only quantifies volume over time; it does not speak to the underlying cause of the surge.

U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.question: What causes the majority of disputes (1785/3025, 59%) tied to ACTUAL-read bills, given tariff, rule-change, AMI-gap, and response-speed hypotheses are all rejected?
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether any bill-correction recommendation or further diagnostic scope should target billing rules, AMI data, or another cause for the ACTUAL-read bucket; blocks scoping recommend_bill_adjustment until resolved.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.resolution_path: Run deeper disputed-bill cause analysis joining billing-db bill detail and DA-RULES change log for ACTUAL-read disputes.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Limit recommend_bill_adjustment scope to ESTIMATED-read disputes only until the ACTUAL-read cause is established.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.resolution: E-10 surfaces BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, no unit scaling comparing raw register value to m3 history) as a specific candidate cause for the ACTUAL/ESTIMATED dispute buckets; magnitude/causal confirmation against actual dispute records is still needed before this unknown can be fully closed.

U-FIELD-DEGRADATION-ROOT-CAUSE.question: Is the field manual-read completion drop (E-03) actually caused by a staffing shortage (E-07) as SH-FIELD claims, or by another factor?
U-FIELD-DEGRADATION-ROOT-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether push_route_update (route priority changes) is the correct corrective action or whether a staffing-level fix outside this solution's scope is needed.
U-FIELD-DEGRADATION-ROOT-CAUSE.resolution_path: Cross-check route-log completion detail against independent field staffing/roster records before relying on the staffing explanation.
U-FIELD-DEGRADATION-ROOT-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Treat the staffing-shortage claim as unverified; do not scope route-priority fixes solely on it without route-log corroboration.

U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.question: Does the currently-inaccessible MDMS AMI export hide any AMI-side contribution to the ACTUAL-read dispute bucket?
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.decision_impact: If MDMS access later reveals AMI-side anomalies, the ACTUAL-bucket cause investigation would need to incorporate AMI read event data not currently reachable.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution_path: Request vendor (ORG-AMI) provisioning of mdms-export access outside the current unavailable-tool window; re-attempt once tool_health reports HEALTHY.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.safe_placeholder: Proceed using billing-db import_status (E-11) as the available proxy for AMI import outcomes; carry the MDMS gap as an acknowledged known limitation (SC-MDMS-ACCESS-LIMITATION).

U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-AS-SUCCESS-PR.question: Does 'dispute volume back to baseline' remain a valid success proxy if ticket-handling changes reduce counts without fixing bill correctness?
U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-AS-SUCCESS-PR.decision_impact: Could cause the solution to be declared successful by suppressing ticket volume (e.g. via auto-answering) while root bill-accuracy causes remain unresolved.
U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-AS-SUCCESS-PR.resolution_path: Validate dispute-volume reduction against read-type dispute share metrics to confirm it tracks bill-correctness fixes, not just ticket suppression.
U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-AS-SUCCESS-PR.safe_placeholder: Keep dispute_volume_baseline as a TARGET, not a MUST, and require corroboration from read-type dispute-share metrics before declaring success.

U-BV17-ACCOUNT-LEVEL-CORRELATI.question: Which specific disputed-bill accounts were actually affected by BV-17's unit-scaling defect, and does that set match the ESTIMATED and ACTUAL dispute buckets observed in E-01?
U-BV17-ACCOUNT-LEVEL-CORRELATI.decision_impact: Determines whether BV-17 is confirmed as the real driver before any recommended correction is scoped, and which accounts a recommend_bill_adjustment should target.
U-BV17-ACCOUNT-LEVEL-CORRELATI.resolution_path: Join billing-db bill/account records flagged by BV-17's high-consumption check against DA-TICKET disputed-bill records to confirm account-level overlap.
U-BV17-ACCOUNT-LEVEL-CORRELATI.safe_placeholder: Ship only a documented, recommendation-only review of BV-17-flagged accounts; no bill writes until correlation is confirmed.

U-ACTUAL-BUCKET-CAUSE.question: What causes the ACTUAL-read dispute majority (1785/3025, 59%, E-01), given tariff, response-speed, field-staffing-magnitude, and BV-17 mechanisms are all ruled out or structurally excluded for it?
U-ACTUAL-BUCKET-CAUSE.decision_impact: Until resolved, no bill-adjustment recommendation can be scoped to the ACTUAL-read bucket; investigation must continue before any corrective action is proposed.
U-ACTUAL-BUCKET-CAUSE.resolution_path: Continue analyze_disputed_bills_by_cause against billing-db bill-detail records for ACTUAL-read disputed accounts, cross-checked with crm-tickets, until a supported hypothesis emerges.
U-ACTUAL-BUCKET-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Report the ACTUAL-read bucket as an unresolved known limitation; issue no bill-adjustment recommendation for it this cycle.

U-BV17-DISPUTE-CORRELATION.question: Do the 1184 accounts flagged by BV-17 (E-11) actually overlap with the 1240 ESTIMATED-type disputed-bill accounts (E-01), confirming BV-17 drives the ESTIMATED bucket at the account level?
U-BV17-DISPUTE-CORRELATION.decision_impact: Confirms or disconfirms whether BV-17 is a material driver of the ESTIMATED-read dispute bucket before any rule-fix or bill-adjustment recommendation tied to BV-17 is proposed.
U-BV17-DISPUTE-CORRELATION.resolution_path: Join billing-db affected_accounts_v42 (BV-17-flagged) against DA-TICKET disputed-bill records restricted to ESTIMATED read type and measure overlap magnitude.
U-BV17-DISPUTE-CORRELATION.safe_placeholder: Treat BV-17's ESTIMATED-bucket contribution as unconfirmed; report rule-change review findings without recommending a fix scope until the join is run.

U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-SUCCESS-VALID.question: Does 'dispute volume back to baseline' remain a valid success proxy if ticket-handling changes reduce counts without fixing underlying bill correctness?
U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-SUCCESS-VALID.decision_impact: If invalid, M-DISPUTE-VOLUME-TREND alone cannot certify success; read-type share metrics must also move favorably.
U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-SUCCESS-VALID.resolution_path: Track dispute volume jointly with read-type share metrics across months; treat volume reduction as valid success evidence only when accompanied by a drop in ESTIMATED/ACTUAL dispute shares tied to a confirmed cause fix.
U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-SUCCESS-VALID.safe_placeholder: Do not treat raw dispute-volume reduction alone as success evidence; require it alongside a confirmed causal fix.

A-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-LINK.statement: The meter-to-cash 'estimate substitution when no accepted read' step is assumed to directly convert the route-completion shortfall (E-03) into the ESTIMATED-type disputed bills counted in E-01, though no evidence directly joins specific disputed-bill records to the shortfall accounts.

A-STAFFING-CAUSES-DEGRADATION.statement: SH-FIELD's claim that a three-reader staffing shortage since July (E-07) caused the route-completion drop is treated as plausible but unverified; the source is non-authoritative and has a disclosed contract-headcount incentive.

A-BV17-DRIVES-BILL-ERRORS.statement: BV-17's unit-scaling defect is assumed to actually generate incorrect bills in the disputed population, not just a theoretical mis-flag risk; no bill-level record yet joins specific disputed accounts to BV-17-affected reads.

A-TIMING-COINCIDENCE-IS-CAUSAL.statement: The exact-month alignment between BV-17's 2026-08-01 deployment and the dispute-volume surge onset is assumed to reflect causation rather than coincidental overlap with an unobserved concurrent change.

A-BV17-ESTIMATED-OVERLAP.statement: The 1184 accounts flagged by BV-17's high-consumption check (E-11) are assumed to substantially overlap with the 1240 ESTIMATED-type disputed bills (E-01) based on matching magnitude; no direct account-level join has confirmed this overlap.

A-REJECTION-TO-ESTIMATE-MECHAN.statement: BV-17's import rejection (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) is assumed to be the proximate cause of the bill_read_type=ESTIMATED outcome for the 1184 flagged accounts via automatic estimate-substitution logic, rather than coincidental co-occurrence.

problem_definition.root_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-05). Response-speed (E-04: within SLA) and tariff-change (E-02, E-06: none logged) causes are ruled out. Billing validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-10), changed the high-consumption check to compare raw register values against 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling; this check rejects AMI imports for flagged accounts (import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) and all 1184 flagged accounts carry bill_read_type=ESTIMATED (E-11), confirming BV-17's import-rejection mechanism converts flagged high-consumption reads into estimate-substituted bills, driving at least part of the ESTIMATED-read disputed-bill bucket (1240/3025, 41%, E-01). Field route-completion shortfall (E-03: 0.88 vs 0.95 target, 9200 accounts) cannot explain this bucket at scale: only 320 accounts were actually marked estimated last cycle (E-09), far below the ~1104 implied by the shortfall. Because BV-17's mechanism structurally produces only ESTIMATED-type outcomes (E-11), it cannot explain the larger ACTUAL-read dispute majority (1785/3025, 59%, E-01), which remains without a confirmed cause after tariff, response-speed, field-staffing-magnitude and BV-17 mechanisms are each ruled out or structurally excluded.

causal_chain: Billing validation rule BV-17 deployed 2026-08-01 changes the high-consumption check to compare raw register values against 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling (E-10).
This check rejects AMI imports for flagged high-consumption accounts, recording import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION for 1184 accounts (E-11).

Per the meter-to-cash 'estimate substitution when no accepted read' step, rejected-import accounts receive an estimate-substituted bill; all 1184 flagged accounts show bill_read_type=ESTIMATED (E-11).
These estimate-substituted bills drive disputes, contributing to the ESTIMATED-read disputed-bill bucket (1240/3025, 41%, E-01) and the dispute-volume surge since August (E-05).

Because this mechanism structurally produces only ESTIMATED outcomes (E-11), it does not reach the larger ACTUAL-read disputed-bill bucket (1785/3025, 59%, E-01), whose cause remains unconfirmed after tariff (E-02/E-06), response-speed (E-04) and field-staffing-magnitude (E-03/E-09) causes are also ruled out or insufficient.

causal_chain: Billing validation rule BV-17 deployed 2026-08-01 changes the high-consumption check to compare raw register values against 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling (E-10).
This check rejects AMI imports for flagged high-consumption accounts, recording import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION for 1184 accounts (E-11).

Per the meter-to-cash 'estimate substitution when no accepted read' step, rejected-import accounts receive an estimate-substituted bill; all 1184 flagged accounts show bill_read_type=ESTIMATED (E-11).
These estimate-substituted bills drive disputes, contributing to the ESTIMATED-read disputed-bill bucket (1240/3025, 41%, E-01) and the dispute-volume surge since August (E-05).

Because this mechanism structurally produces only ESTIMATED outcomes (E-11), it does not reach the larger ACTUAL-read disputed-bill bucket (1785/3025, 59%, E-01), whose cause remains unconfirmed after tariff (E-02/E-06), response-speed (E-04) and field-staffing-magnitude (E-03/E-09) causes are also ruled out or insufficient.
